note: Golden retrieval set for `fxlla kb eval`. The corpus is this repository's own documentation: real technical prose about distinct topics, no invented fixtures and no network. Queries are phrased as a person would ask them rather than as keyword lookups, so they exercise the embedding rather than string overlap. `expect` lists every file that legitimately answers the query; a hit is any of them appearing in the top k. Scores compare models against each other at one commit; they are not comparable across commits, because editing the docs changes the corpus.

queries.q: I found a vulnerability, how should I report it without making it public?
is it safe to let other machines on my network reach the model endpoint?
who has the final word when the maintainers disagree?
what do I have to do to get write access to the repository?
which version of bash do the scripts have to run under?
am I allowed to use emojis or em dashes in the source?
how many commits should pile up before I ask for a review?
which languages can the user interface be translated into, and where do the strings live?
where is the only file allowed to hold my Hugging Face token?
how do I get tab completion working in my shell?
what has to be installed before any of this works?
how can I tell whether a model is already downloaded to disk?
why was Apple's MLX rejected as the engine for embeddings?
what went wrong when the code graph was ported to KuzuDB?
what work is still sitting in the backlog?
how does the router pick which loaded model to throw out when memory runs short?
why does this tool deliberately not implement its own agent loop?
what shipped in the first tagged release?
